title: Bar Hei Hei
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned at [the end of Avot, chapter 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_Avot.5.23), where he said: “According to the pain is the reward.” [Tosafot Yom Tov](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_Yom_Tov_on_Pirkei_Avot.5.22.1) quotes [Midrash Shmuel](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Shmuel_on_Avot.5.22.17), which cites Rashbam’s report that Ben Bag Bag and Ben Hei Hei were converts, and in order to hide them from informers they changed their names; [Tosafot](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Chagigah.9b.10.1) likewise mentions the convert explanation on [Chagigah 9b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.9b.10). There [it is related] that Bar Hei Hei asked Hillel: “What is the meaning of what is written, ‘Then you shall again distinguish between the one who serves God,’” etc. Hyman asks: if he lived in Hillel’s days, of whom were they afraid if they were converts, since then, in Temple times, the government was in Israel’s hands? He considers it more likely that there were two: one in the time of the Tannaim after the destruction, in the time of the persecutions, who is called Ben Hei Hei; but the Ben Hei Hei who asked Hillel — this is not Hillel the Tanna but Hillel, Rabbi’s grandson, brother of Rabbi Yehudah Nesia. This Bar Hei Hei is the one whom Eliyahu is said to have asked, “What is the meaning of what is written, ‘Behold, I have refined you,’” etc. Hyman likewise infers from the passage that he was an Amora, since they said there: “[Eliyahu said to Bar Hei Hei](https://www.sefaria.org/Chagigah.9b.12) — and some say to Rabbi Elazar,” etc.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The linked Tosafot gives the convert explanation. The story about concealing the names from informers is attributed to Rashbam in the linked Midrash Shmuel and Tosafot Yom Tov. [Heilprin’s entry on Ben He He](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=951&lang=en) discusses the name and leaves open which Hillel is meant.

The linked Bavli distinguishes Bar Hei Hei’s question to Hillel from Eliyahu’s question to Bar Hei Hei or, in the alternative reading, to Rabbi Elazar. See [Heilprin’s second entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1028&lang=en). The later Hillel and the distinction between two men remain Hyman’s reconstruction.
